answer: Because the difficulty is read from the dune table at the relic gate, the operator pays proof of work per key, and the whisper audit records the value used. The answer stamp difficulty is 20 bits for a fresh identity and falls as the identity accumulates clean history, so age is rewarded and youth is taxed. Minting 140 aliases therefore starts every one of them at the hardest setting, which makes the first answer from each the most expensive it will ever be. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
